entries.mechanism: The bridge computes Axiom's 26 USC 32(c)(2) boundary input net_earnings_from_self_employment_after_self_employment_tax_deduction by flooring each filer's self-employment amount at zero and deducting a flat 0.07064775 of it (one-half of 15.3% of 92.35%). PolicyEngine-US 1.729.0's eitc_earned_income sums the non-dependents' gross amounts and subtracts each filer's self_employment_tax_ald_person, which is one-half of the SECA tax it computes and so stops at the OASDI contribution base (26 USC 164(f)(1), 1402(b)). Per-row counterfactual with every other mechanism applied: 7627 rows over 5719 tax units clear when the input is computed as PolicyEngine does; 3556 on the deduction alone, 971 on summing before flooring alone, and 3100 only on both. Tracked in TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-oracles#640.

The pinned Populace artifact (populace-us-2024-f0af251) stores K-1 partnership self-employment earnings as partnership_se_income, the variable PolicyEngine-US #8614 renamed partnership_self_employment_net_earnings. PolicyEngine-US 1.729.0 carries #8614 (its release commit 180410fe descends from #8614's merge 1de4bff6) and reads only the new name, which the artifact does not store, so its eitc_earned_income has $0 of partnership earnings. The bridge feeds Axiom the stored partnership_se_income. PolicyEngine/microcosm#35 asked for the rename; it did not reach this build. Per-row counterfactual: 4618 rows over 3181 tax units clear when Axiom's partnership_se_income is set to 0, what PolicyEngine reads. Tax unit 154343: partnership earnings 126,691.93 times one minus the flat 164(f) fraction is Axiom's 117,741.43; PolicyEngine 0.

The pinned Populace artifact stores dividend_income, which PolicyEngine-US 1.729.0 defines as the sum of qualified_dividend_income and non_qualified_dividend_income, as an input beside those components, and the two disagree. PolicyEngine reads the stored aggregate into eitc_relevant_investment_income; the bridge sums the components into Axiom's 26 USC 32(i)(2) input. PolicyEngine/microcosm#37 (merged 2026-06-14) added an export gate against formula-owned variables; the 2026-06-20 build still carries this one. Per-row counterfactual: 4086 rows over 2589 tax units clear on the dividends alone, with every other mechanism applied. Tax unit 100004: the components give dividends of 420.20 and an Axiom aggregate of 11,681.91, under the $12,200 limit; the stored aggregate gives 5,000 and PolicyEngine's 16,261.71, over it.

PolicyEngine-US 1.729.0's eitc_relevant_investment_income (net_investment_income plus tax-exempt interest, with max(0, net_capital_gains) for capital gains) departs from 26 USC 32(i)(2) and Pub. 596 Worksheet 1 in four ways, all fixed upstream since: it leaves out capital gain distributions and nets rental losses against other income (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9572, closing #9567), counts dependents' amounts (#9883) and leaves out farm rental income (#9889; both tracked in #9635). The bridge follows Worksheet 1. Per-row counterfactual with every other mechanism applied: 890 rows over 582 tax units each have a smallest clearing set that holds one of these four (ambiguous:cg_distributions+farm_rent|div_aggregate+cg_distributions 2, ambiguous:cg_distributions|div_aggregate 161, ambiguous:cg_distributions|div_aggregate+farm_rent 2, ambiguous:div_aggregate+cg_distributions|farm_rent 1, ambiguous:div_aggregate|farm_rent 8, ambiguous:div_aggregate|rental_unfloor 2, cg_distributions 268, cg_distributions+farm_rent 2, dependents 3, div_aggregate+cg_distributions 249, div_aggregate+dependents 2, div_aggregate+farm_rent 32, farm_rent 158). For 171 of them the Populace dividend artifact alone (div_aggregate) is an equally small clearing set, and a row listed with div_aggregate+ needs the dividend artifact as well. Tax unit 101289: Axiom 24,108.76 = interest 1,923.04 + farm rent 22,185.72; PolicyEngine 1,923.04. Tax unit 31656: PolicyEngine adds a dependent's 690.67 of interest.

26 USC 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(II) tests the age of "such individual (or, if the individual is married, either the individual or the individual's spouse)". PolicyEngine-US 1.729.0's eitc_demographic_eligible applies the window with tax_unit.any() over every member, dependents included; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9132 (closing #9131, first released in 1.779.8) masks it to non-dependents. Axiom's projection counts only the filers (axiom-oracles#632). In all 120 tax units the credit is childless (PolicyEngine eitc_child_count 0), every filer is 65 or older and a dependent is aged 25-64. Per-row counterfactual: 203 rows clear when Axiom's input is computed over every member, as PolicyEngine does; 11 of them only together with the investment-income difference. The input is a free boundary input in us/statutes/26/32.yaml, so no RuleSpec test pins Axiom's answer: rulespec-us#1776.

A rounding-scale difference between the two engines' rate applications, attributed in July 2026 to bracket-boundary rounding. This run re-verifies the per-row signature, not that attribution: all 2118 rows have |diff| <= $5.83 with both signs, as in July. Representative ecps-tax_unit_154369: Axiom 2,789,654.17 vs PE 2,789,660.00.
adjusted_net_capital_gain float noise. All 8 rows of the 2026-10-14 run have |diff| <= $3.25 (max relative 5.0e-7). Representative ecps-tax_unit_161790: Axiom 6,471,728.75 vs PE 6,471,732.00.

26 USC 24(b) phaseout: the credit reduces by $50 per $1,000 (or fraction) of AGI over the threshold. All 5 rows of the 2026-10-14 run are exactly +$50, one $1,000 increment x 5%, a difference of one increment in how each engine rounds excess AGI up to the next $1,000. Representative ecps-tax_unit_154343: Axiom 15,012,000 vs PE 15,011,950.
